newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin takes first stroll since pneumonia-doctor.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin takes first stroll since pneumonia-doctor.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin took his first stroll outdoors on Tuesday since falling ill with pneumonia two weeks ago, chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Reuters.

"Today for the first time he went outside and went for a walk at his country residence. He went around the house and talked to the people at home with him. When we arrived he was talking to his youngest grandson. It was a lively conversation," said Mironov, speaking an hour after seeing Yeltsin.

Mironov stressed that Yeltsin, who moved on Monday evening to his Gorky-9 residence near Moscow after 12 days in hospital with double pneumonia, was in a "completely satisfactory condition" and had worked for over seven hours on Tuesday.

"It's fairly stressful work, government documents. He's not only signing them but correcting them," Mironov said. "He had work-related calls with his aides. Today he had a very fruitful loaded work day. I left him about 6 p.m. (1500 GMT) and he wasn't in bad shape."

"Double pneumonia requires a rather long treatment with medicines. But now on the whole the medicines are aimed at strengthening the body and contributing to erasing the effects of an internal infectious pneumonia...It's a matter of time."

Mironov said Yeltsin was "morally worn down" by going back into hospital just two weeks after returning to the Kremlin following his six-month lay-off for heart surgery. He was now "convalescing physically and morally" but Mironov warned that he would be prone to fatigue for a time and had to take life easy.
